evals.prompt: Break Cambridge A-level Data Representation into an infographic learning path. Keep it knowledge-first, use syllabus only for an internal concept-family coverage check, and estimate a sensible number without treating it as fixed. Do not put syllabus references on the artwork plan.
evals.expected_output: An ordered, concept-led topic map with learner questions, explicit boundaries, provisional count, internal coverage separated from learner-facing content, and no assumption that one objective maps to one infographic.
expectations: The proposed sequence is organized around learner questions and conceptual dependencies rather than syllabus objective order.
The count is explicitly provisional, and split/merge decisions use explanation and readable density.
Any curriculum coverage audit is clearly internal and no syllabus markers are proposed for artwork.
The byte definition is stated plainly without irrelevant history.

evals.prompt: Plan a short infographic series explaining how a web browser loads a page for first-year learners. I have no syllabus in mind; keep the map focused on the conceptual dependencies and say what should be researched before drawing.
evals.expected_output: A learner-oriented sequence with one distinct question per proposed infographic, dependency order, a provisional granularity rationale, and research seeds clearly distinguished from verified facts.
expectations: The topic map has an understandable dependency order and distinct learner questions.
The estimate is provisional and the granularity rationale is explicit.
Facts that need research are marked as seeds rather than asserted as verified.
